aliases.reason: A kernel ideal is the inverse image of zero under a unital homomorphism of commutative rings; the same prerequisite is used for small extensions, formally smooth local algebra surjections and general algebra kernels. Their square-zero or module-length conditions are extra source constraints. The full source phrase 'kernel ideal of source ring homomorphism' was checked against canonical 'I=ker(P→S)'; original additional hypotheses are preserved.

A kernel ideal is the inverse image of zero under a unital homomorphism of commutative rings; the same prerequisite is used for small extensions, formally smooth local algebra surjections and general algebra kernels. Their square-zero or module-length conditions are extra source constraints. A square-zero ideal J is exactly an ideal whose products of all pairs vanish (J²=0). Being the kernel of a particular algebra map or being inside an R-algebra is an additional source context, not a different definition of square-zero. This does not alias all nilpotent ideals, only exponent two. The full source phrase 'square-zero condition on its kernel ideal' was checked against canonical 'square-zero ideal I²=0'; original additional hypotheses are preserved.
